page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. It includes hardware-assisted instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations and memory throughput. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the middle 50% of tested systems, though single-core stress-ng performance registers in the lower 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average capabilities, with read-only large block transfers reaching 96.6 GB/sec and write operations at 55.45 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also align with mid-range expectations, processing 14.1 million operations per second.

This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external network-attached block storage. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-16 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance local disk I/O or GPU acceleration.

The resource profile of this server makes it suitable for memory-intensive applications such as medium-sized databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks. It is also appropriate for static web serving and lightweight language model inference, though it is less suited for compute-heavy single-threaded tasks or large-scale AI model training.
